OWGAP — the showcase experiments

Hidden-vitality synthetic experiments for confounding-robust policy optimization. Observed fitness X, unobserved vitality S with P(S=+1|X)=σ(10X); vitality dominates outcomes (±8–9) while the true treatment effect is a few units and therapy carries a fixed burden. One discrete and one continuous experiment, plus real-data validation. The question throughout: do the odds-box ∩ Wasserstein (O-W) methods recover the oracle policy where naive and box-only methods fail? Built Sun Jul 26 15:19:32 PDT 2026.

1. The data-generating process

Aggressive therapy under hidden vitality, with a fixed therapy burden: fitness X is observed, vitality S is unobserved, Y is the outcome (higher is better). N=600 per seed unless stated.

X~Unif{−1,−23,…,1} (7 levels; continuous variant: X~Unif[−1,1]),S∣X∈{±1},  P(S=+1∣X)=σ(10X)
T∣X,S~Bernoulli(e(X,S)),e(X,S)=clip(σ(0.8S−2X),0.02,0.98)
μ0=8S,μ1=9S+3X−1,Y(t)=μt+𝒩(0,0.62)
CATE(X)=(2σ(10X)−1)+3X−1⇒oracle treats iff X>0,CATE(0)=−1

S shifts both arms by ±8–9 while the treatment differential is a few units: treated patients look great because they are vital, not because therapy works. The -1 is a fixed treatment burden (toxicity/cost), so over-treatment is visibly bad (all-treat = -1). The true selection odds ratio is Λ=e2·0.8=4.95, so Γ=5 is the matched sensitivity level — results quoted "at matched Γ" involve no tuning. Reference values: never-treat 0, all-treat -1, oracle 0.847 uncapped / 0.727 under the 30% capacity cap (the cap is genuinely scarce: 30% < the 43% oracle-treat mass).

Where the confounding bias lives (a design feature, stated up front). Selection on S operates at every X (the 0.8S term in the propensity), but it can only BIAS a within-X comparison where X fails to pin down S — i.e. where Var(S|X) = 4p(1-p) with p = σ(αX) is non-negligible. At the strong coupling α=10 this is the σ(αX)≈½ region: on the 7-level grid, the X=0 level (naive CATE inflation +6.5; faint traces ±0.8 at X=±1/3); in the continuous variant, a band |X|≲0.2 that shifts the naive decision threshold. This concentration is the unavoidable consequence of ANY monotone X–S coupling crossing one-half, not a planted artifact; the continuous experiment shows the band version of the same effect, and the coupling sweep (Discrete tab, Section 3) shows what happens as the region widens.

P(S=+1 | X) = σ(10X). Var(S | X) = 4σ(10X)(1-σ(10X)), maximal at X=0.

CATE(X) = E[Y(1) - Y(0) | X] = (2σ(10X)-1) + 3X - 1; oracle π*(X) = 1{CATE(X) > 0}.

P(T=1 | X,S) = clip(σ(0.8S - 2X), 0.02, 0.98); Λ = exp(2·0.8) = 4.95.

2. Design rationale: why the burden and the scarce cap exist

The DGP above was reached by an explicit design iteration, worth reporting because it explains what the experiment isolates. A first, burden-free variant (μ1 = 9S + 1.5X, i.e. THETA=0, so CATE(0)=0, with a loose 50% cap) produced the same estimation failure but a muted experiment: the naive methods' signature error is treating X=0 — the one level where S is genuinely uncertain given X, so within-level selection inflates the estimated CATE from -1 (there: ~0) to ~+5.5 — but with CATE(0)=0 that error was COSTLESS uncapped, and under the loose cap the trimming even rescued the naive methods ("cap-rescue": margins +0.104 uncapped, +0.056 capped). The final DGP keeps the entire structure and makes exactly that error expensive:

μ1=9S+3X−1⇒CATE(X)=(2σ(10X)−1)+3X−1,CATE(0)=−1

plus a genuinely scarce budget: cap 30% < the 43% oracle-treat mass. Unchanged by the redesign: coupling, propensity (so Λ=4.95 and matched Γ=5), oracle = treat iff X>0, uncapped oracle 0.847, never-treat 0. New: all-treat = -1. (A burden-free variant rerun at N=1000 also confirmed the O-W margins are not a small-sample artifact.)

Black: CATE(X). Brown: the infinite-data naive limit E[Y | T=1, X] - E[Y | T=0, X]; the difference is confounding bias, non-negligible only at X=0 (-1 → +5.5).

Why each method will pick its policy (predictions under test). Naive IPW/AIPW: over-credits therapy at X=0 (vitality-enriched treated arm) → treats it first; uncapped this buys CATE=-1 harm, capped it wastes a third of the budget. Box-only O-X at Γ=5: worst-case collapses toward never-treat (no balance constraint to anchor mass). Kallus: same box, same collapse. O-W: the Wasserstein constraint forces the reweighted X-distribution to stay close, and since X tracks S (α=10 regime, where Section 5 says balance works), the worst case cannot fabricate vitality gaps → recovers "treat the fit" at both caps. A continuous twin with the same constants is defined in exp_owgap_v2_cont (x* = 0.137, oracle 0.737, naive DR threshold shifts to -0.29). Results: see the Discrete tab, Section 1; every prediction above was confirmed.

0. Problem setup, methods, and protocol

We learn an individualized treatment rule π(X) ∈ [0,1] from observational data (Xi, Ti, Yi) whose treatment assignment depended on an unobserved confounder S, maximizing the policy value

V(π)=𝔼[π(X)Y(1)+(1−π(X))Y(0)],π*=\argmaxπV(π)

Because e(X,S) is not identified from (X,T,Y), plug-in ("naive") methods carry hidden-confounding bias. The robust methods optimize the worst case over an uncertainty set of inverse-propensity weights: the marginal sensitivity model (odds-box, "O") bounds how far the true propensity odds may deviate from the fitted observable propensity,

Γ−1≤e(X,S)/(1−e(X,S))e^(X)/(1−e^(X))≤Γ

and the Wasserstein covariate-balance constraint ("W") additionally requires the worst-case reweighted treated and control covariate distributions to stay within transport cost ϵ of each other (ϵ set data-driven as cϵ times the tightest feasible value):

𝒲(∑iwi(1)δXi,∑iwi(0)δXi)≤ε

Evaluation protocol

Matched Γ. Every DGP has a known true selection odds ratio Λ; headline numbers are quoted at Γ = Λ (no tuning), with full Γ-curves showing misspecification behavior. Value. Discrete experiments report exact (noise-free) policy value on the level grid; continuous experiments report realized test value on fresh draws with known potential outcomes, deploying support policies off-support via the Shapley extension (closed-form Lipschitz min-max interpolant, exact at the support points). Uncertainty. Mean ± SD over seeds, plus paired per-seed 95% CIs for the headline margins. Ablations. Coupling strength α (when does balance help), transport budget cϵ, capacity budget (30/40/50%), and the Lipschitz constant L (continuous).

1. Headline results: N=600, 20 seeds, both regimes

The showcase DGP (DGP tab, Sections 1–2) at N=600, 20 seeds, cε=1.0. At the matched Γ=5 the O-W margin over the best naive method is +0.122 uncapped and +0.150 capped (the burden-free design variant gave +0.104 / +0.056 — the capped margin tripled once the X=0 mistake carried a real cost). The external Kallus & Zhou baseline (box-only, parametric softmax; uncapped only, since a smooth policy class cannot enforce a hard capacity) peaks at 0.18 near Γ=1 and collapses to never-treat by Γ≈2.5 — the box alone forces total pessimism; only the Wasserstein balance constraint lets robustness coexist with a non-trivial policy.

2. Selected policies: π(X) vs X for every method and Γ (mean over 20 seeds)

Tick any set of methods to overlay them, then pick a Γ and the regime; the plot shows each selected method's policy as treatment probability π(X) over the 7 levels, averaged over all 20 seeds, with the oracle for that regime as the dashed reference (uncapped oracle (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1), capped(30%) oracle (0, 0, 0, 0, 0.1, 1, 1)). With a single method ticked, the exact π vector is printed under the plot.

overlay methods:

What to look for: the naive X-X curves do not move with Γ (plug-ins ignore it) and always treat the selection-inflated X=0 level (true CATE = -1); the box-only O-X curves drain toward never-treat as Γ grows — worst-case pessimism with nothing to anchor it — and Kallus drains the same way; the O-W curves stay anchored near the oracle across the whole Γ range, hedging only the ambiguous X=0 level. Under the cap the question becomes WHERE each method spends its 30% budget: O-W concentrates it on the top levels, the naive methods burn roughly a third of it on X=0. This Γ-stability of the selected policy — not just of the value — is the Wasserstein constraint's visible fingerprint.

3. Coupling sweep: when does O-W win?

The X–S coupling α in P(S=+1|X)=σ(αX) is swept over {1,2,4,6,10} (N=600, 8 seeds, cε=1.0, on the burden-free outcome variant — the coupling and propensity are identical to the showcase DGP, so the boundary transfers) while the true selection strength is held FIXED at Λ=4.95: only the usefulness of X as a proxy for S varies.

α=60.810.8170.6370.692+0.055

Honest scoping: the margin flips sign. O-W wins for α≥6 (corr(X,S)≳0.8), roughly ties at α=4, and LOSES below that — at weak coupling the Wasserstein constraint has nothing to grab (balancing X no longer balances S) and matched-Γ robustness over-hedges below never-treat. This is a boundary of applicability, not graceful degradation. Diagnostic upside: corr(X, S-proxy) is measurable, so the operating regime is checkable in practice — and the Real-data tab's Experiment B shows the diagnostic passing on the actual Diabetes coupling (corr≈0.20, correctly predicted out-of-regime).

1. The L × Γ surface: continuous X and the Lipschitz constant

The showcase DGP with continuous X ~ Uniform(-1,1) (identical constants to the discrete experiment; oracle threshold x*=0.137, oracle 0.737, never-treat 0.018, all-treat -0.959; naive DR baseline 0.390). N=400 train, 4000 test, 8 seeds; off-support deployment: the Shapley extension (closed-form Lipschitz min-max interpolant, exact at the support points). With per-unit policies (L=∞) every support point is its own parameter: the policy overfits and Γ is inert. Two dials fix it: the Lipschitz class |π(x)-π(x')| ≤ L|x-x'| for the VARIANCE, and Γ robustness for the BIAS. The L × Γ surface shows both.

Best overall: DoublyRobust-O-W at Γ=8, L=3 → 0.548. The full seed-0 policy curve for EVERY (Γ, L) cell of this surface is shown in Section 2 below.

2. Policy curves: π(x) vs x for every method, Γ, and L

The complete answer to "what policy did each method actually pick": choose a method, a Γ, and a Lipschitz constant L, and the plot shows the seed-0 learned policy π(x) over x ∈ [-1, 1] for that cell of the Section-1 surface, deployed off-support via the Shapley extension (closed-form Lipschitz min-max interpolant, exact at the support points). Dashed references: the oracle (treat iff x > 0.137) and the naive DR plug-in (threshold shifted left to ≈-0.3 by hidden-vitality bias: it over-treats the ambiguous band). Unlike KNN averaging, this deployment is exact at the support points, so the L=∞ curves show the per-unit overfitting oscillation directly rather than a smoothed band.

Verification plot. The first panel shows the RAW pointwise solver output: the 400 per-unit values π(Xi) that the LP actually chose at the training support (seed 0; faint brown dots = the naive plug-in's raw 0/1 decisions). The second panel is the same policy after off-support extension. Because the Shapley operator is exact at support points, the extended curve must pass through the dot cloud wherever the plot grid comes close to a support point — at L=∞ both panels oscillate together, and at L≤3 the dots already lie on a smooth ramp that the extension simply traces. Any systematic gap between the two panels would indicate an extension bug.

overlay methods:

What to look for as you move the dropdowns: at L = ∞ the curve is jagged — per-unit policies overfit each support point, and changing Γ barely moves them (the inert-Γ column of the surface). At moderate L (1.5–3) the curve is a clean step whose boundary sits near the oracle's. Raising Γ drains the box-only O-X curves toward π≡0 (worst-case collapse to never-treat), while the O-W curves keep a stable treat-region — the Wasserstein anchor at work; their boundary drifts only slightly right (more conservative) with Γ. Best overall cell: DoublyRobust-O-W at Γ=8, L=3.

Real data: UCI Diabetes 130-US Hospitals (69,990 patients)

Covariate X = composite frailty score (age, medications, length of stay, labs, procedures), rescaled to [-1,1]; hidden confounder S = acuity (prior inpatient/ER visits, diagnoses, facility discharge), median-split; treatment T = the real insulin decision (53% treated). The REAL X–S coupling is weak: corr(X,S)=0.196, matched Γ=1.26 — by the coupling-sweep diagnostic (Discrete tab, Section 3) this dataset sits OUTSIDE the O-W operating regime. We therefore run two complementary experiments rather than forcing a win:

Experiment A — in-regime semi-synthetic (real covariates, simulated confounding). Real bootstrapped X (real covariate geometry); S ~ Bern(σ(12(X-0.07))) calibrated to the real acuity rate 0.249 with E[Var(S|X)]=0.23 (comparable to the owgap α=10 regime); T synthetic with the real fitted X-coefficient, real treated fraction 0.51, and selection strength CS=0.8 giving Λ=4.95 — the SAME matched-Γ=5 protocol as owgap. Outcomes: μ0=-3S, μ1=-1.5S+X-0.3 (sicker patients do worse in both arms; insulin helps the sicker and frailer, minus a fixed burden). The failure mode is the mirror image of owgap: sicker patients get insulin AND do worse, so the naive plug-in concludes insulin is harmful and treats NOBODY (naive = never-treat 1.51 vs oracle 1.78, oracle treats the frailest 21%). Together the two experiments show both classic confounding failures — over-treatment (owgap: hidden vitality flatters the drug) and under-treatment (here: hidden acuity damns it) — each corrected by the same O-W machinery.
Experiment B — fully real (X, S, T): the diagnostic validation. Everything real except the calibrated synthetic potential outcomes (needed for ground truth). With the real weak coupling the linear-naive gap is only 0.001 (naive ≈ oracle) and the matched Γ is 1.26: the scoping diagnostic PREDICTS robustness is unnecessary here. Running the full method suite and observing exactly that — naive fine, O-W at matched Γ harmless, large Γ over-hedging — validates the diagnostic on real data and shows the method does no harm outside its regime.

Experiment A results (in-regime)

Oracle 1.763, never-treat 1.491, all-treat 0.268, naive DR 1.507. Best overall: DoublyRobust-O-W at Γ=3, L=3 → 1.699. Kallus best 1.471.

Verdict A: prediction confirmed. The naive plug-in (1.504) sits essentially at never-treat (1.491) — it concluded insulin is harmful and treated almost nobody, the classic under-treatment failure. The robust methods recover ~75% of the naive-to-oracle gap (IPW-O-W 1.697, DR-O-W 1.702 at L=3, Γ=3–4; margin +0.19 over naive), while the parametric box-only Kallus baseline lands BELOW never-treat (1.471). On real covariate geometry with in-regime confounding, the correction works in the under-treatment direction just as it does in owgap's over-treatment direction. Box-only O-X variants perform close to O-W here (1.69) at their best Γ — the Wasserstein term's decisive advantages remain the discrete capped regime and stability across Γ (see the other tabs); on this axis the honest claim is "all Γ-robust methods fix the failure; O-W is never worse".

Experiment B results (fully real)

Oracle 1.284, never-treat 1.248, all-treat 0.804, naive DR 1.268. Best overall: IPW-O-X at Γ=1, L=2 → 1.264. Kallus best 1.231.

Verdict B: the diagnostic passes on real data. With the real weak coupling, naive DR (1.268) is already near-oracle (1.284) — a gap of 0.016. Every robust method's optimum sits at Γ=1 (≈ the real matched Γ=1.26) with value 1.263 ≈ naive: robustness at the matched level does NO harm. Raising Γ strictly degrades value (1.258 → 1.201 at L=3) — the over-hedging the coupling diagnostic predicts out-of-regime. Together with the α sweep this closes the loop: the measurable coupling diagnostic tells practitioners when the O-W machinery pays off, and real data behaves exactly as it forecasts.
